text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria is expected to peg the lev to the the German mark from July 1 as part of preparations to introduce a fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Economic policy minister Krassimir Angarski said. @
-- More than 850 firms from 36 countries have confirmed their participation in Bulgaria's International Trade Fair in Plovdiv which opens today, officials said.

-- Bulgaria's pro-reform Union of Democratic Forces which won a clear majority in the April 19 elections is expected to hold a second round of consultations with other parties in the new parliament on a declaration for national concensus on ways of leading the country out of crisis.
-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry said it had prevented an attempt on the lives of Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov and his Romanian counterpart Emil Constantinescu on April 30. @
Police officers had found some 700 grammes of TNT explosive planted near the Sofia airport an hour before the two presidents drove by in a Mercedes car.
-- Bulgaria has invited a Romanian delegation to Sofia at the end of May to discuss the location of a planned second bridge over the Danube river, Bulgaria's Transport Ministry officials said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to propose to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to raise its assumption for the average salary in the public sector to $150 by the year-end because of the recent lev stability against the dollar, Social Care Minister Ivan Neikov said.
Average salary in the public sector was projected at $65-70 in the funding accord with the IMF signed in March.

-- France's Banque Credit Agricole was ready to extend some $60 million loan to Bulgaria to fund setting up garbage recycling plants in the country's three biggest cities of Sofia, Plovdiv and Varna, private Balkan agency said. @
-- Bulgaria's Socialist Party (BSP) elected its leader Georgi Parvanov as a chairman of BSP's parliamentary group.
